Amram et al.</td><td>2025</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="amram-2024fjg-detail" data-tags="open data|foundation models"><td colspan="3">

Aspen Open Jets, about 178 M jets from CMS 2016 open data, for pre-training foundation models.

Derives about 178 M high-$p_T$ jets from CMS 2016 open data and pre-trains the OmniJet-α foundation model on them. Pre-training on collision data improves the generation of the simulated top and QCD jets of JetClass despite the domain shift.

<tr class="row" id="elitez-2025aqs" data-tags="reconstruction"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="elitez-2025aqs-detail">ColliderML: The First Release of an OpenDataDetector High-Luminosity Physics Benchmark Dataset</button></td><td>D. Elitez et al.</td><td>2025</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="elitez-2025aqs-detail" data-tags="reconstruction"><td colspan="3">

ColliderML, one million fully simulated HL-LHC events in the OpenDataDetector, for detector-level machine learning.

Experiment-agnostic collisions at 14 TeV with a mean pile-up of 200, across ten Standard Model and beyond-Standard-Model processes plus single-particle samples, fully simulated, digitised and reconstructed, and published on Hugging Face.

<tr class="row-detail" id="govorkova-2021hqu-detail" data-tags="anomaly detection|real-time inference"><td colspan="3">

A simulated trigger-level event stream for unsupervised new-physics detection at 40 MHz.

Emulates the data stream of a real-time event-selection system, pre-filtered by requiring an electron or muon, so that new selection strategies and their sensitivity to new phenomena can be developed under trigger constraints.

<tr class="row" id="komiske-2019jim" data-tags="open data|jet tagging"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="komiske-2019jim-detail">Exploring the Space of Jets with CMS Open Data</button></td><td>P. T. Komiske et al.</td><td>2020</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="komiske-2019jim-detail" data-tags="open data|jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

Jets from CMS 2011 open data, and the metric space of jets measured with the energy mover's distance.

Isolates 1,690,984 central jets with transverse momentum above 375 GeV from 2.3 fb⁻¹ of 7 TeV CMS open data and compares them with simulation. The energy mover's distance between jets is used to study the space of jets and the effect of the detector.

<tr class="row" id="krause-2024avx" data-tags="fast simulation|generative models"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="krause-2024avx-detail">CaloChallenge 2022: a community challenge for fast calorimeter simulation</button></td><td>C. Krause et al.</td><td>2025</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="krause-2024avx-detail" data-tags="fast simulation|generative models"><td colspan="3">

The Fast Calorimeter Simulation Challenge 2022, 31 generative models compared on four shower datasets.

Compares variational autoencoders, GANs, normalizing flows, diffusion and flow-matching models on showers from a few hundred to tens of thousands of voxels, by shower quality, generation time and model size. Quality is measured with histograms, KPD and FPD scores, classifier AUCs and a multiclass classifier.

<tr class="row-detail" id="atlas-2024rua-detail" data-tags="jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

Performance and systematic uncertainties of machine-learning top taggers in full ATLAS simulation.

Evaluates several machine-learning top taggers on simulated 13 TeV ATLAS events and estimates their systematic uncertainties with an approximate procedure. The dataset, with its systematic variations, is public.

The FAIR Universe HiggsML Uncertainty challenge, confidence intervals from imperfect simulators.

Participants reported confidence intervals for a parameter of interest of the Higgs boson while accounting for systematic uncertainties, on a tabular dataset of 280 million simulated collisions with 28 features.

<tr class="row-detail" id="bukhari-2023ezc-detail" data-tags="neutrino physics|reconstruction"><td colspan="3">

The three winning solutions of the IceCube Kaggle competition.

Describes the data handling, architecture and training of each and compares them on the Kaggle dataset. The best reaches an angular resolution better than 5° for cascades above 10 TeV and better than 0.5° for tracks, comparable to the state of the art.

Scalable graph and transformer models for particle flow in full simulation of e⁺e⁻ collisions.

Compares a graph neural network with a kernel-based transformer on tracks and calorimeter clusters. The best model improves the jet transverse momentum resolution by up to 50% over the rule-based algorithm.

<tr class="row-detail" id="qu-2022mxj-detail" data-tags="jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

The Particle Transformer and the JetClass dataset of 100 M jets in ten classes.

The Particle Transformer adds pairwise particle interactions to the attention mechanism and surpasses a plain Transformer and ParticleNet; pre-trained models improve other tagging tasks after fine-tuning.

Finds existing point-cloud GANs inadequate for jets and evaluates generated jets with Wasserstein distances, a Fréchet ParticleNet distance, coverage and minimum matching distance.

<tr class="row-detail" id="pata-2021oez-detail" data-tags="reconstruction"><td colspan="3">

MLPF, end-to-end particle-flow reconstruction with graph neural networks.

A scalable graph-network algorithm that reconstructs particles from tracks and calorimeter clusters, aimed at high pile-up and shown on a Delphes simulation with an average pile-up of 200.

<tr class="row" id="shlomi-2020ufi" data-tags="reconstruction|jet tagging"><td><button type="button" class="row-toggle" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="shlomi-2020ufi-detail">Secondary vertex finding in jets with neural networks</button></td><td>J. Shlomi et al.</td><td>2021</td></tr>
<tr class="row-detail" id="shlomi-2020ufi-detail" data-tags="reconstruction|jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

A set-to-graph network that finds secondary vertices inside jets.

Decides for every pair of tracks in a jet whether they share a vertex, using all the jet's tracks. It outperforms traditional vertex finding and improves bottom-versus-charm flavour tagging.

<p class="row-tags"><button type="button" class="tag" data-tag="reconstruction">reconstruction</button><button type="button" class="tag" data-tag="jet tagging">jet tagging</button></p>

<tr class="row-detail" id="andreassen-2019cjw-detail" data-tags="unfolding"><td colspan="3">

OmniFold, unbinned unfolding of all observables at once by iterative reweighting.

Uses classifiers to reweight a simulated dataset iteratively, so that every observable is unfolded without binning, including those not yet defined at the time of the analysis. Illustrated on jet substructure.

<tr class="row-detail" id="moreno-2019bmu-detail" data-tags="jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

JEDI-net, jet identification with interaction networks over the jet's constituents.

Needs no special handling of sparse inputs, no particle ordering and no assumption about the detector geometry, and reaches better results with fewer parameters.

<p class="row-tags"><button type="button" class="tag" data-tag="jet tagging">jet tagging</button></p>

<tr class="row-detail" id="moreno-2019neq-detail" data-tags="jet tagging|open data"><td colspan="3">

Interaction networks over tracks and secondary vertices to identify boosted H → bb̄ jets.

Describes the jet as particle-to-particle and particle-to-vertex interactions. Trained on CMS simulation released on the CERN Open Data Portal, it improves markedly on the algorithms of its time.

<tr class="row-detail" id="komiske-2018cqr-detail" data-tags="jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

Energy and Particle Flow Networks, permutation-invariant networks for jets built on Deep Sets.

Energy Flow Networks are infrared and collinear safe by construction; Particle Flow Networks admit general energy dependence and particle information such as charge and flavour. The quark and gluon jets used in the paper are public.

<tr class="row-detail" id="butter-2017cot-detail" data-tags="jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

A top tagger built on Lorentz vectors and the Minkowski metric.

Uses calorimeter towers and tracking information, and outperforms QCD-inspired and image-based taggers for strongly boosted top quarks.

<tr class="row-detail" id="duarte-2018ite-detail" data-tags="real-time inference|jet tagging"><td colspan="3">

<tr class="row-detail" id="paganini-2017dwg-detail" data-tags="fast simulation|generative models"><td colspan="3">

CaloGAN, generative adversarial networks for showers in a multilayer electromagnetic calorimeter.

Achieves speed-ups of 100 to 1000 over full simulation on CPU and up to about 10⁵ on GPU, and reproduces geometric shower-shape properties of photons, positrons and charged pions.
